scope: Curated scholarly descriptions and annotation motifs, NOT a transcription or independent decipherment
provenance_policy: Each passage links to a public text or scholarship. Editorial motif tags are hypotheses to be audited against original languages.

items.period: Second century BCE composition; surviving witnesses later
items.witness: Ancient composition transmitted in multiple traditions; use critical editions
items.claim: The narrative says angels taught Noah plant-based remedies and Noah recorded and transmitted the knowledge to Shem.
items.caution: The angels are not named Raphael in this Jubilees passage; manuscripts and verse numbering differ.

items.work: Prologue to Sefer Asaf ha-Rofe (in Jellinek's Sefer Noah)
items.locus: Medical prologue / Book of Remedies introduction
items.period: Early medieval composition; surviving manuscript tradition later
items.witness: Later Hebrew text; Jellinek compilation contains distinct compositions
items.claim: Prologue attributes post-Flood medicinal revelation to Raphael and says Noah passed a recorded book to Shem.
items.caution: A medieval retrospective account, not independent proof of an antediluvian source or a continuous manuscript chain.

items.period: Late antique magical treatise, surviving in later textual tradition
items.claim: Preface attributes a book of mysteries given by Raziel to Noah immediately before the Flood.
items.caution: Distinct pre-Flood revelation and angel from the post-Flood Raphael medicinal account.

items.period: Likely third or early second century BCE; date debated
items.witness: Specific Noah-book phrase extant in a Greek excerpt, not surviving Aramaic Qumran pieces
items.claim: References a book attributed to Noah in connection with blood and priestly instructions.
items.caution: Uncertain whether 'concerning blood' is part of the book title; NOT evidence of blood medicine.

items.period: First-century BCE/CE manuscript; underlying composition earlier
items.witness: Qumran Cave 1 Aramaic scroll; title-reading partly reconstructed
items.claim: Preserves a probable heading for 'Book of the Words of Noah' followed by first-person Noah material.
items.caution: The initial word in the reading is restored; does not identify a book of medicines.

items.witness: Ancient textual versions including Qumran fragments
items.claim: Raphael guides Tobias regarding fish organs used in the narrative for exorcism and healing.
items.caution: No claim that Tobias used Noah's medical book; ancient ritual narrative, not medical advice.

items.witness: Aramaic fragments with lacunae and contested interpretation
items.claim: Fragmentary Aramaic anti-demonic material related to bodily and domestic concerns.
items.caution: No title or attribution to Noah; manuscript restoration and interpretation disputed.

items.period: Manuscript copied in first century CE
items.claim: Collection of songs/psalms associated with protection against demons, including Psalm 91.
items.caution: No Noah book claim; this is genre-context evidence only.

items.period: Coptic manuscript fourth century CE; composition date debated
items.claim: Shem receives a cosmic revelation concerning primordial powers and a retelling of the Flood.
items.caution: No surviving claim to preserve Noah's medical remedies or lost medical book.
